items.title: Delhi protests: Supreme Court declines to entertain challenge to Section 163 BNSS
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday declined to entertain a challenge to the constitutional validity of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which empowers executive magistrates to issue prohibitory orders to restrict public gatherings in the interest of preventing danger or maintaining peace. The Court, however, has agreed to examine various prohibitory orders issued under the said provision in connection with the recent Delhi protests. The Court will also examine a challenge to the validity of Section 172 of the BNSS, which requires persons to comply with lawful directions issued by police officers and gives the police the power to detain those who defy such directions and obstruct police duties. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi yesterday sought the response from the Central government, the Delhi government, the Delhi Commissioner of Police and other authorities on a plea challenging this provision.
